highlights.summary: Computer scientist, entrepreneur, and philanthropist will collaborate with the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing to advance AI and scientific discovery.
body: David Siegel SM ’86, PhD ’91, a computer scientist, entrepreneur, and philanthropist, will serve as the next MIT Innovation Fellow during the 2026-27 academic year. Working with the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing, Siegel will explore how artificial intelligence can accelerate scientific discovery at the Institute and beyond.

“From the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing to the MIT Siegel Family Quest for Intelligence, David has been a superb thought partner for me and other Institute leaders on a range of very significant initiatives, so we're delighted to have him join us now as an MIT Innovation Fellow,” says MIT President Sally Kornbluth. “Our community has long benefited from David's exceptional technical insight, entrepreneurial experience, instinct for connecting people, and infectious love for MIT. We look forward to working with him now as he helps us identify new opportunities at the intersection of AI and scientific discovery.”

body: England's three-Test series against South Africa will take place across December and January, marking England's first Test tour of South Africa in seven years.
The series follows England's first-ever home Test series whitewash of Pakistan and will be Stephen Fleming's first series in charge as England men's Test head coach.

The Test series will be followed by three ODIs in January, as England prepare for the ICC Men's World Cup 2027, which will take place across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia in October and November next year.

Sky Sports will broadcast live coverage of a packed schedule of international cricket from South Africa, with Australia men's tour getting under way this Thursday with the first of three ODIs in Durban, followed by three Tests.

highlights.title: A24's Wild Documentary You Can See Everything Gets First Bizarre Trailer
highlights.summary: Nathan Fielder has built a career on absurd stunts that make it almost impossible to tell fact from fiction. His first major series, Nathan for You, was a reality TV show that parodied shows like Shark Tank, with Fielder playing an elevated, awkward version of himself who gave horrible business…
body: You Can See Everything is an upcoming documentary co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim that centers on Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of the disgraced health technology company Theranos. A24 produced the movie, and it was shot in the weeks before Holmes began serving her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The movie's runtime is a meaty 174 minutes.

From the trailer, we see many of Fielder’s trademarks, such as an interrogation of the line between performance and truth. His dry sense of humor and tendency to drag absurdity out of his subjects are on display when he bluntly points out to Holmes’ partner that she may have conned him out of his wealth. The film's co-director, Lance Oppenheim, is an experienced documentarian who just released his first feature-length drama, the highly anticipated Primetime ​​​​​​from A24. Fielder has also partnered with A24 in the past, starring in the dark comedy TV series The Curse.

highlights.title: ‘Today’ Snares Top Two Positions in Morning-News Battle for First Time in 14 Years
highlights.summary: NBC’s “Today” is back on top in TV’s never-ending morning wars. The A.M. news franchise finished the 2025-26 broadcast season with the most viewers overall among morning programs and the most viewers between the ages of 25 and 54, the demographic most coveted by advertisers in TV-news content.
body: “Today” captured an average of 2.938 million viewers for the season, 4%, or 114,000 viewers higher, than audience levels at ABC’s “Good Morning America,” according to data from Nielsen, and 67%, or 1.174 million higher than viewership at “CBS Mornings.” Overall, the audience for “Today” rose by 7%, or 185,000 viewers, over the previous season.

“Today” won an average of 609,000 viewers between 25 and 54, 28%, or 134,000 more than “GMA” and 120%, or 332,000 more than “CBS Mornings.” It is the largest share of the demographic captured by the show in 15 years, according to data from Nielsen.

One ever-present dynamic of TV’s morning-news battle is that it never ends. “Today” will have to contend with not only its usual competition from “GMA,” but a new lineup at CBS, where Norah O’Donnell has rejoined the network’s A.M. team.

highlights.title: Eric Idle has had tons of celebrities staying at his house. God, it must be exhausting | Adrian Chiles
highlights.summary: Whether it’s an A-lister or an old schoolfriend emerging blearily from the spare room, those first moments of the day are tricky. First thing in the morning, that’s the hardest time. Eric Idle told me this. A wise man, is Eric.
body: This isn’t an issue raised in the book, which I should say is a moving, elegiac affair, and not just a torrent of name-drops as I’ve rather implied. But the guest question nagged away at me until I plucked up the courage to interrogate Mr Idle on the matter. Who was the best guest? Who was the worst? And what did he do if they were getting on his wick? After all, since they’d gone all that way, he could hardly turf them out.

Sensibly, Eric wouldn’t be drawn on any of these questions, although much as he plainly loved them being there, he did tacitly admit that having guests in your space – even guests of this calibre – does have its challenges, and that it’s the mornings that are hardest.

highlights.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
highlights.summary: OpenAI is extending access to its Daybreak program to the Government of Ukraine to support the cyber defense of civilian infrastructure.
body: The announcement was made on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly by Dmytro Kushneruk, the Consul General of Ukraine in San Francisco, and Sasha Baker, Head of National Security Policy at OpenAI.

Ukrainian defenders face persistent cyber attacks from Russia, alongside physical attacks on the country’s infrastructure. Ukraine’s national cyber incident response team, CERT-UA, handled ⁠ (opens in a new window) nearly 6,000 cyber incidents in 2025. These include attacks on hospital systems, the energy sector and telecommunications, underscoring the pressure on the organizations providing essential services to Ukrainians.

OpenAI’s Daybreak gives cyber defenders access to advanced AI for authorized security work, from reviewing older software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities and testing fixes.

highlights.title: Trump lawyers defend president banning journalists from White House ahead of court hearing – live
highlights.summary: Trump lawyers say White House access is ‘a privilege, not a right’; CNN, Politico and MS Now to present case in court after president banned outlets from White House grounds. Sign up for US Breaking News emails.
body: In a new legal filing in the case over a trio of new outlets barred entry to the White House, Trump administration lawyers repeatedly defended the president’s ban by saying journalists were not entitled to access to the building.
“Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right,” the filing stated.

The filing went on to assert that the three outlets – by publishing sensitive or classified information obtained through its reporting – constituted a national security threat, giving the president the right to ax their credentials.

Trump banned the three outlets – CNN, MS Now, and Politico – last Friday in a snap decision announced via social media. He branded the three outlets “fake news” and threatened future bans against other outlets could follow.

body: Hamilton and Ferrari's hopes of winning this years world title have faded in recent races, with the Briton not finishing on the podium since the British Grand Prix at the start of July.

A first race retirement of the season last time out in Madrid saw third-placed Hamilton fall over 100 points back on championship-leading Kimi Antonelli for the first time this season, with the seven-time champion all-but conceding the title.
Antonelli's overall lead at the top of the standings is 81 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
Asked about his own championship prospects heading into weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the season's 15th of a scheduled 23 rounds, Hamilton said: "Well, I mean, he's 101 points ahead of me.

body: Alongside the season’s other big looks – balloon pants, jaunty hats, the rogue use of scarves, knee-length skirts and underwear-as-outerwear – it’s clear the mood in fashion is messy-but-chic. Not quite the luxurious chaos of early 2000s boho, but similarly pretty and off kilter.

Thankfully, given the state of the economy and the environment, for the most part this style can be achieved by reaching into the dark corners of your wardrobe and looking at forgotten items with fresh eyes. Here, four fashion professionals explain how.

Figuring out exactly what is in your wardrobe is a worthwhile exercise at the change of seasons. Pull everything out and examine each item – this gives you the opportunity to rediscover pieces you’ve stopped wearing and to clean, mend or alter anything that could go back into rotation after a bit of love and care.

highlights.title: Two years of OpenAI Academy
highlights.summary: Marking two years of OpenAI Academy and bringing AI skills to even more communities.
body: Building on our work to help people develop practical AI skills, with plans to bring training to more communities.

To ensure the benefits of AI are broadly shared, people need the skills and confidence to use it in their everyday lives. Since launching in September 2024, OpenAI Academy has helped people build those skills through practical training for tasks ranging from teaching and running a small business to developing software.

Over the past two years, OpenAI Academy has hosted more than 250 events, and more than 4 million people have engaged with Academy content. That work has brought together educators, small business owners, developers, nonprofit leaders and community members to learn, practice, and share what works.

For this next chapter, we’re expanding OpenAI Academy through a new trainer program that prepares people and organizations to teach Academy material in their communities. This program builds on our work with partners and will make training and ongoing support available closer to where people live and work.
points: Marking two years of OpenAI Academy and bringing AI skills to even more communities.

highlights.title: Can Arteta turn champions into serial winners?
highlights.summary: When Mikel Arteta signed his last Arsenal contract in September 2024, his quest to bring major silverware back to the club was ongoing. Two years later, he agrees his new one after leading them to a long-awaited Premier League title.
body: Mikel Arteta has agreed a new contract as Arsenal manager following their Premier League title triumph last season; Gunners boss has overseen a remarkable transformation of the club since his arrival in 2019, so can he build on their success?

Arteta has overseen a total transformation of the club since his appointment in 2019. Arsenal, 10th in the Premier League table when he took over, were in a state of drift. Now, they are re-established among Europe's elite, unrecognisable in all departments.

Arteta has joined a select group of 13 managers to have won the Premier League. He now has the chance to join an even smaller group, made up of only Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger, by winning it more than once.
Securing a first Champions League, after guiding Arsenal to only their second final last term, is another chance for immortality.

body: Before the festivals began, I posed a question: How divisive (or bad) would “Digger” need to be for Tom Cruise to lose this season? Venice, Telluride and Toronto have come and gone and now we approach the moment of truth. But there’s a more interesting question percolating — what will a Cruise Oscar campaign ask the Academy to recognize?

“Digger” stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy tycoon who must save the world when one of his oil rigs malfunctions and causes an environmental catastrophe across the planet. The film also includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons. The social embargo that lifted on Sept. 22 was mixed, with many praising Cruise’s performance but coming down hard on the film’s ultimate execution.

highlights.title: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them
highlights.summary: Part of the job of a content creator is to figure out how to get their work in front of the most people. Cracking - or fighting - the algorithm has historically been a frustration for creators, but YouTube is increasingly simply telling creators what they should do.
body: YouTube wants creators to use its own tools to optimize their content to break through.

At the annual creator-focused Made on YouTube event, the company announced updates to the suite of AI-powered creator tools it unveiled in 2025. In its initial iteration, the dashboard of creator tools included things like A/B testing for video thumbnails and a chatbot interface to query how content was performing. This year’s update adds AI tools for more complex tasks.

Perhaps most significantly, YouTube is introducing an AI “agent” that will work in the background to optimize a creator’s channel. For example, the tool will monitor a creator’s back catalog of videos, looking for content that has taken on a new life, is relevant to the news, or has started trending. The agent will offer suggestions for tweaking the thumbnails or titles for older videos to ride the new wave of relevance. The tool can also put together things like pitches for brands by combing through a creator’s YouTube channel and pulling out demographic and audience data to make a case to potential sponsors, says Amjad Hanif, vice president of creator products at YouTube.

highlights.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli tells BBC Sport how he is "still finding my way" in F1 after a 2024 crash "stayed in my head for a very long time".
body: Kimi Antonelli says he knew from the first moment he drove this year's Mercedes that he would be transformed as a Formula 1 driver in 2026.
The 20-year-old Italian, who is running away with the world championship in only his second season in F1, is reflecting on his breakthrough year in the sport in an exclusive interview with BBC Sport.

A difficult debut season last year had left external expectations of Antonelli low at the start of 2026. But on a typically damp and cold January day at Silverstone, he already sensed that something special might be on the cards.

"It was just a few laps in the wet," Antonelli says, "but I just felt better in the car, much better than I felt last year. Also the car felt well, but I just felt better mentally in the car. Less tense, more relaxed and more mature."

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation says it knows of five crashes in which drivers using…
body: Comma.ai was the brainchild of George Hotz, who rose to prominence at the start of the last decade by jailbreaking iOS and hacking Sony PlayStations. In 2015, Hotz turned his attention to partially automated driver assists, which were gaining attention following Tesla’s exploits with its Autopilot system. Hotz first modified his own Acura to give it a more advanced driver assist that let him take his hands off the wheel, with the goal of selling his system to Tesla and replacing Mobileye as the company’s supplier.

Comma’s first attempts to sell devices that owners could plug into their cars’ ODB port evaporated once NHTSA began asking questions in 2016. Instead, Comma decided to post its openpilot software, as well as its plans for hardware, to GitHub, allowing anyone to make the devices themselves. At first, the Comma Neo and OpenPilot supported a single Acura and single Honda model, but by 2020, the company’s software and $999 device were rated more highly by Consumer Reports than any OEM system.

highlights.title: AT&T Is Automating Away Jobs—and Its Old Telecom Empire
highlights.summary: The telecom giant is eager to show Wall Street that it can do more with less. That means fewer employees, less electricity, and increased automation.
body: AT&T, which already shed more than half of its workforce over the past decade, says it's going to continue laying off staff as it gears up for the AI era. The telecommunications giant is also doing away with its old-school landline service and using artificial intelligence to automate some internal processes. All this downsizing is resulting in tangible benefits, including a considerable decrease in electricity usage, AT&T chief technology officer Jeremy Legg tells WIRED.

“We’re not going to have the same headcount in five years as we do today,” Legg says, adding that comparing its staffing levels to that of peers plays a role in its decisionmaking. According to public financial disclosures, AT&T generated less revenue per employee last year than its competitors Verizon and T-Mobile, both of which have let go of workers in recent months.

body: That makes for a long list, but the biggest surprise, as pointed out online, is that Nintendo is literally older than sliced bread. Technically, this would make sliced bread the best thing since Nintendo, and for double-technicality points, we're referring to commercial pre-sliced bread. According to the history books, pre-sliced bread made its commercial debut 38 years later, on July 7, 1928, when the Missouri-based Chillicothe Baking Company began using Otto Frederick Rohwedder's bread-slicing machine to deliver tasty portions of the household staple to customers.

Today, Nintendo is worth many billions of dollars thanks to the release of several highly successful consoles, including the Wii and the Switch. In recent years, it has also intensified its efforts to be more than just a video game company, launching new theme parks and slowly releasing more feature film adaptations based on its original IP.
The two Super Mario Bros. movies developed by Illumination have each grossed north of $1 billion at the box office, and the next project is a live-action Legend of Zelda movie.

body: Amanda Kernell's third feature brings the identity politics of her debut, the historical drama 'Sámi Blood,' into the present day.

If Kernell’s screenplay can feel a bit schematic in its funneling of wider social issues into the small, hard story of one individual, “Brace Your Heart” is otherwise played with pleasing, powerful restraint — beginning with Valkeapää’s quietly expressive performance of a naturally taciturn character. highlights.title: Why fans are digging their claws into Wolverine over its patronising gameplay
highlights.summary: From highlighted ledges to characters telling you what to do, blockbuster games are increasingly taking the challenge out of playing – and players are pushing back. • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: It is hand-holding to the point of parody. Indeed, it reminded me of the sniggersome Mario in Unreal Engine satirical videos that makes the social media rounds every few months (“A mushroom? I should take a look at this”). Skill Up’s clip has been followed by hundreds of others, gleefully ripping into Wolverine with ironic savagery. In one much-copied clip, a streamer simply lays down his controller during a motorbike chase sequence and watches as Wolverine speeds on regardless, bouncing off the scenery as the game plays itself.

People really detest this kind of thing. It’s impossible to pinpoint exactly when big-budget games started assuming that players were irredeemably stupid, but throughout the late 00s and 2010s it became more and more common to see obvious GPS trails showing you where to go, and for characters to talk to themselves to remind you what to do. At the same time, there’s been a cyclical discussion over the difficulty of games: every time a notably challenging game comes out, we rehash the same talking points about whether all games should have easy modes. Is it acceptable for games to shut players out if they aren’t prepared to “git gud”?

Announced at this year’s Made On YouTube event, the updates include “Ask Music,” a conversational tool for music and podcasts, and “Your Podcast Lineup,” a personalized audio guide designed to help listeners discover new shows.

Built directly into the YouTube Music app, Ask Music lets users describe what they want to hear in everyday language rather than searching for individual songs or artists. The feature works across YouTube Music’s catalog of more than 300 million songs, including official recordings, remixes, live performances, covers, and DJ sets. highlights.title: LA 2028 triathlon course will see athletes race from Venice Beach into Pacific
highlights.summary: Women’s triathlon will award first medals of Games. Beach start only second in Olympic triathlon history. The first medals of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics will be doled out on the eclectic confines of Venice Beach, where organizers have unveiled a triathlon course that will send athletes racing…
body: LA28 unveiled initial details of the Olympic and Paralympic triathlon routes on Wednesday, laying out a compact course through Venice that takes in the beachfront bike path, neighboring streets and the Venice Canals before finishing overlooking the coastline.

The women’s individual triathlon on 15 July 2028 will produce the first medals of the Games, one day after the unprecedented dual-venue opening ceremony at the the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. The men’s race follows on 16 July, with the mixed relay on 20 July.

In a departure from the usual Olympic setup, the individual races will begin on the beach rather than from a pontoon. It will be only the second beach start in Olympic triathlon history, following the 2016 events at Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach, with athletes sprinting from the sand directly into the Pacific. They will complete a two-lap 1,500m swim – an opening 1,000m circuit followed by a 25m run along the beach and a second 500m swim.

These problems can’t be something that Marvel and Disney are too happy about, especially since Avengers: Doomsday, which is almost certain to be a financial success, is only a few short months away and could generate a large influx of new players. highlights.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: in praise of slightly silly clothes
highlights.summary: The push to buy lasting, sustainable clothes is a good thing, but every wardrobe need a bit of mischief. I do hope you are wearing your zebra stripe trousers today. Anyone who is anyone is wearing zebra stripes this month, you know.
body: Only teasing. Fashion doesn’t work like that any more. The days when people like me bullied everyone else into wearing banana yellow one season and puffball sleeves the next are over. Looking trendy is over. Timeless chic is the only show in town. Peacocking has been phased out in favour of understatement and personal style.

This is a very good thing. The fashion playbook that minted a whole new look every six months has a lot to answer for, seeding a sense of clothes as disposable that has got us into the right old mess that the industry is now in, with a glut of poorly made garments. Clothes that you never tire of, that you look after and repair because you want to wear them for ever, are obviously the holy grail of a sustainable wardrobe. When a look has the timestamp of a specific season – like Brat green in the summer of 2024 or Barbie pink the year before – it becomes a sell-by date. Clothes have a longer shelf life when their appeal isn’t based on novelty.
points: The push to buy lasting, sustainable clothes is a good thing, but every wardrobe need a bit of mischief.
